newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Canberra calls for union apology over riot.
newsitem.headline: Canberra calls for union apology over riot.

text.p: Australian Treasurer and Acting Prime Minister Peter Costello said on Wednesday the Australian Council of Trade Unions (ACTU) should apologise for the violence at an ACTU-organised rally in Canberra on August 19.
"I think what the ACTU should have said was that we organised the demonstration, we apologise for the violence, we accept responsiblity for it," Costello told Melbourne radio 3AW.
On Tuesday the ACTU said it was not responsible for the actions of what it called a small minority at the rally of trade unionists outside the Federal parliament.
The ACTU said it condemned the violent actions of some demonstrators who stormed the building and clashed with police because they undermined the collective objectives of the union movement.
The rally was called by the ACTU to oppose the government's plan to free up the labour market, which the unions say will weaken their influence.
